subject.title: [Bug]: browser upload/file chooser flow is flaky and can misreport stale-click failures as browser control timeouts

question: Should Browser upload remain an explicit caller-supplied `ref`/`inputRef`/`element` API, or should OpenClaw add an owner-approved atomic upload-trigger behavior that re-resolves the trigger and aligns timeout diagnostics?
rationale: Current main has partial mitigations but the remaining change affects the model-facing Browser tool contract and the reliability semantics of file upload actions on dynamic pages.

options.title: Keep open for Browser owner design
options.body: Settle the upload-trigger contract and live repro requirements before asking automation to implement a fix.

options.title: Narrow timeout-only repair
options.body: Fix the 20s file-chooser wrapper timeout first while leaving atomic trigger behavior for a separate decision.

options.title: Treat selector/batch as sufficient
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide the supported path is selector/batch plus stale-ref recovery instead of atomic upload-trigger behavior.

recommendation.title: Keep open for Browser owner design
recommendation.body: Settle the upload-trigger contract and live repro requirements before asking automation to implement a fix.

likelyOwner.reason: He is both the current issue assignee and the strongest Browser plugin history owner in the traced files.
